paper.title: Risk-sensitive Bandits: Arm Mixture Optimality and Regret-efficient Algorithms

unmapped: Objective is a distortion riskmetric U_h of the empirical mixture of arm distributions; regret = V(alpha*,F) - E[V(tau_T/T,F)], compared against the best mixture of arms (not a single arm)
Rewards are positive-valued, 1-sub-Gaussian; DR bounded by B; U_h Hölder continuous (exponent q) and mixture-Hölder (exponent r)
Learner needs the minimum discrete sub-optimality gap Delta_min(eps) over the discretized simplex and the Hölder parameters q, L
settings.definition_quote: for a given policy $\pi$ and horizon $T$, we define the regret as the gap between the DR achieved by the oracle policy and the \emph{average} DR achieved by $\pi$, i.e., \mathfrak{R}_{\bnu}^\pi(T)\triangleq V(\balpha^\star, \F) - \E_{\bnu}^\pi[V(\frac{1}{T}\btau_T^\pi, \F )]

symbols.L_H: unified Hölder constant max{L_H, L_MH} of the DR
symbols.W: max ratio of Wasserstein to L1 distance between arm mixtures (W <= sqrt(2 pi))
symbols.q: Hölder continuity exponent of U_h, in (0,1]
symbols.M_eps: N(eps)/log T, exploration-length constant depending on Delta_min(eps), K, L, q

conditions: U_h Hölder continuous with exponent q
regret measured on the distortion riskmetric of the empirical arm mixture
tuning: exploration length N(eps) as in eq. (number of samples), using Delta_min(eps)

source.label: theorem: ETC upper bound
source.quote: For any $\varepsilon\in\R_+$ and distortion function $h$ with H\"older exponent $q$, for all $T>N(\varepsilon)$, RS-ETC-M's regret is upper bounded as \mathfrak{R}_{\bnu}^{{{\rm E}}}(T) \leq (\mcL K + W^{-q}) \bigg(3 WM(\varepsilon)\; \frac{\log T}{T} \bigg)^q + \Delta(\varepsilon).

results.notes: Regret is defined on the DR of the average mixture (already normalized, not a sum over rounds); not multiplied by T. Comparator is the best arm mixture; 'best_fixed_action' used as nearest vocabulary term.

symbols.beta_gap: gap exponent beta = lim log Delta_min(eps)/log eps

tuning: eps = Theta((K^{2+2/q} T^{-gamma} log T)^{q/(2 beta)})

source.label: theorem:RS-ETC-M
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem \ref{theorem: ETC upper bound}, when $\beta$ exists, the minimum feasible regret RS-ETC-M satisfies is \mathfrak{R}_{\bnu}^{{\textnormal{\rm E}}}(T) \leq O(([K^{c_{\rm E}}\cdot \frac{\log T}{T^{\gamma}}]^{\frac{qr}{2\beta}})), where $c_{\rm E}\triangleq {2(1+\frac{\beta+1}{q})}$ and $\gamma = \frac{2\beta}{2\beta+r}$.

results.notes: Specializations in Table 1 (e.g. O(log T/T) for mean, CVaR, dual power; Gini deviation etc.) not recorded separately.

symbols.B_dr: upper bound B on the distortion riskmetric

conditions: U_h Hölder continuous with exponent q

source.label: theorem:UCB upper bound
source.quote: For any $\varepsilon\in\R_+$, and distortion function $h$ with \holder exponent $q$, for all $T>\max\{\e^K,T(\varepsilon)\}$, for $\pi\in\{{\rm U,C}\}$ we have \mathfrak{R}_{\bnu}^{\pi }(T) \leq [B + \mcL(W^q+1)] [\frac{64}{\sqrt{\varepsilon \rho T}}( \sqrt{2\e\log T} + 32)]^q + \Delta(\varepsilon).

results.notes: RS-UCB-M involves optimization over distribution confidence sets (paper calls it computationally expensive); compute marked exponential tentatively. Regret already normalized by T.

conditions: U_h Hölder continuous with exponent q

results.notes: Same statement as r3 for CE-UCB-M. The appendix proof for CE-UCB-M actually derives a slightly different constant (5 L K W (32 ...)^q); recorded as in theorem. CE-UCB-M is described as computationally tractable but per-round cost is over the discretized simplex (size ~eps^{-(K-1)}).

source.label: corollary:RS-UCB-M
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem \ref{theorem:UCB upper bound}, when $\beta$ exists and $r \leq \beta + \frac{q}{2} $ the regret upper bound for $\pi\in\{{\rm U,C}\}$ is \mathfrak{R}_{\bnu}^{\pi}(T) \leq O (K^{c_{\rm U}} [\frac{\log T}{T}]^{r \kappa} ), where $c_{\rm U}\triangleq \max\{ r(1+ \frac{2\kappa}{q}),{1-\kappa} \}$.

results.notes: Table 1 specializations (e.g. O((log T/T)^{1/4}) for mean/CVaR under Bernoulli) not recorded separately.
